gaps.sentence: I am afraid you ___ park here without a resident's permit.
gaps.hint: permission that is refused with cannot

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.

gaps.sentence: I ___ help thinking he is hiding something.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't help' plus -ing means being unable to stop a feeling: can't help thinking.

gaps.sentence: I ___ have said that — I apologised immediately.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' expresses regret about a past action: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to be at the airport three hours before long-haul flights.
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' shows obligation from outside the speaker: have to be.

gaps.sentence: Need we ___ the whole report, or just the summary?
gaps.hint: modal need takes the bare infinitive
gaps.explanation: When 'need' is a modal in questions and negatives, it takes the bare infinitive: read.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well tell him the truth — he will find out anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests doing something because there is no reason not to: might as well.

gaps.sentence: I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.
